stories.body: The United States urged allies and China to join an economic campaign to isolate Iran, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent promising what he called the toughest sanctions in history and warning countries that maintain economic ties with Tehran. The push comes amid stalled US-Iran talks and a sharp fall in shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, where only seven commodity vessels reportedly crossed on Thursday as security concerns deterred traffic on the vital energy route.
stories.headline: US launches economic pressure campaign against Iran as Hormuz shipping traffic drops

stories.body: A Hong Kong court found activists Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung guilty of incitement to subversion for their roles in the now-disbanded Hong Kong Alliance, which organised annual candlelit vigils commemorating the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown. The pair, who pleaded not guilty, could each face up to 10 years in prison; sentencing will take place later. Rights groups condemned the case as an example of the national security law's broad use against dissent, while authorities maintain the law is necessary for stability.
stories.headline: Hong Kong Tiananmen vigil organisers convicted on national-security charges

stories.body: The Panama Canal Authority will reduce daily transit capacity to 34 vessels from early September and to 32 from 15 September as drought linked to El Niño lowers the freshwater supplies required to operate the locks. The canal normally accommodates about 40 ships a day and handles roughly 5% of global maritime trade. Authorities say the restrictions are intended to conserve water from Gatun Lake, which also supplies nearby cities, while reduced transit capacity could slow shipping and raise costs.
stories.headline: Panama Canal to restrict vessel traffic as El Niño drought worsens

stories.body: North Korea launched about 10 short-range ballistic missiles toward its eastern waters, according to South Korea's military, a day after the United States and South Korea scaled back their Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises. President Donald Trump had ordered a substantial reduction in the drills, citing his relationship with Kim Jong-un, but Kim's sister Kim Yo-jong said their provocative nature would not change and dismissed the move as insufficient. Seoul convened an emergency security meeting and said it was coordinating closely with the US and Japan.
stories.headline: North Korea fires missiles after Trump scales back US-South Korea drills

stories.body: A Russian overnight missile and drone attack on Kyiv killed at least 16 people and wounded around 40, Ukrainian authorities said, damaging a children's hospital, a school, a nursery and other civilian sites. Ukraine said Russia launched dozens of ballistic, cruise and hypersonic missiles as well as 168 drones; air defences intercepted 145 drones and most cruise missiles but could not stop ballistic missiles. President Volodymyr Zelensky described the assault as among the war's most cynical and large-scale attacks and called for a stronger international response and more anti-ballistic defences.
stories.headline: Russian missile barrage kills at least 16 people in Kyiv

stories.body: Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Canada condemned Israel's decision to issue tenders for 1,234 homes in the E1 area of the occupied West Bank, calling for the plans to be withdrawn immediately. The project lies between East Jerusalem and the settlement of Maale Adumim and critics say it would split the West Bank, isolate Palestinian-majority East Jerusalem and severely undermine the prospect of a contiguous Palestinian state. The UN secretary-general also warned that the plan posed an existential threat to such a state; Israel disputes the international legal assessment of its settlements.
stories.headline: European governments condemn Israel's planned E1 West Bank settlement project

stories.body: The United States imposed sanctions on nine Cuban state-owned mining, metals and construction companies, the Construction Ministry, and officials linked to the Cuban Institute of Friendship with the Peoples. Secretary of State Marco Rubio accused those targeted of supporting Cuba's repression and of promoting Marxism and anti-American activities abroad. Cuba's foreign minister, Bruno Rodríguez, condemned the measures, saying they would further damage an economy already struggling to provide basic services amid fuel shortages and prolonged power cuts.
stories.headline: Trump administration expands sanctions on Cuba

stories.body: Half of Americans, including nearly a quarter of Donald Trump's 2024 voters, say his mass-deportation campaign is too aggressive, according to a Politico poll conducted from 8 to 12 August. That result was largely unchanged from earlier polling despite the administration reducing high-profile raids and emphasizing arrests of people accused of crimes. The survey found a significant split within Trump's coalition: 31% of non-MAGA Trump voters called the campaign too aggressive, compared with 15% of self-identified MAGA voters, highlighting a potential Republican vulnerability before the midterms.
stories.headline: Poll finds persistent concern over the aggressiveness of Trump's mass-deportation campaign

stories.body: Newly released emails show that US Immigration and Customs Enforcement officials coordinated with Iranian authorities on three deportation flights that returned more than 100 Iranians between September 2025 and January 2026. The correspondence, obtained by the National Iranian American Council and first reported by The Intercept, indicates Iranian officials requested changes to flight manifests and that ICE made at least some adjustments. The cooperation continued despite rising tensions between Washington and Tehran and internal acknowledgement that some Iranians were fleeing the aftermath of the June 2025 US-Israel war with Iran.
stories.headline: Newly released emails reveal ICE-Iran channel that shaped deportation flights

stories.body: Texas Governor Greg Abbott has targeted airport facilities used for Muslim ritual washing, prompting legal experts to dispute his claim that the stations are discriminatory. Critics told The Washington Post that the move fits a broader pattern of anti-Muslim rhetoric and actions by Abbott and other Republican officials.
stories.headline: Texas governor targets Muslim washing facilities at airports

stories.body: Spanish police removed between 1,500 and 4,000 migrants from an improvised camp on El Trampolín beach in Ceuta and transferred them to newly prepared sites at Loma Margarita and Loma Colmenar, which the government says can house 1,800 people. The evacuation was largely peaceful, but around 500 people later returned to the beach, with many Moroccan migrants saying they feared deportation if they entered official facilities. Spain is expanding temporary shelters after the mass border crossing from Morocco in late July, while political tensions over the response continue.
stories.headline: Spain relocates migrants from Ceuta's El Trampolín beach amid a continuing humanitarian crisis

stories.body: Spanish law requires unaccompanied migrant children to receive the same basic protection, healthcare, education and social services as Spanish children, and does not permit their automatic collective return, legal experts say. Repatriation may be considered only through an individual process that hears the child and assesses family reunification or suitable protection in the country of return, with the child's best interests paramount. The European Commission said Spain has a duty to protect vulnerable minors, even as it reiterated the EU's expectation that migrants who entered Ceuta irregularly should be returned to Morocco in accordance with EU and international law.
stories.headline: Spain faces renewed political and legal dispute over protection of unaccompanied migrant children in Ceuta

stories.body: Catalonia's civil protection agency has activated the Inuncat emergency plan as storms are forecast to bring intense rain through Saturday, with more than 40 litres per square metre possible in 30 minutes in some areas. Meteocat also warned of hail, wind gusts above 90 km/h and possible tornadoes, while storms on Thursday brought fallen trees, minor flooding and around 50 calls to firefighters in an hour. Authorities have urged residents to avoid flood-prone streams and ravines, and red flags were raised at several beaches because of rough seas.
stories.headline: Heavy rain alerts issued across Catalunya as storms move in

stories.body: Barcelona is expected to see a marked change in weather, with scattered showers possible during Friday and the greatest risk of heavy rain, hail, strong wind and thunderstorms from Friday evening into Saturday morning. A cold upper-level trough meeting accumulated heat and warm Mediterranean water could produce locally torrential downpours, although the heaviest rain may fall south of the city. Temperatures are expected to ease, with daytime highs around 28-29C and cooler nights over the weekend.
stories.headline: Barcelona braces for potentially intense overnight rain and cooler temperatures

stories.body: Barcelona Metro's L1 service between Florida and Plaça de Sants is scheduled to resume on 29 August after a six-week closure for track and workshop upgrades. TMB has replaced 1.58km of ballast track with more stable concrete track between Santa Eulàlia and Mercat Nou, renovated parts of the century-old Santa Eulàlia workshop, and upgraded related infrastructure. The €11.5 million project is intended to reduce vibrations, maintenance needs and service incidents; replacement buses will continue until 28 August.
stories.headline: Barcelona's L1 Metro works near completion ahead of service restoration on 29 August

stories.body: Barcelona's deputy mayor Laia Bonet said the Save Europe Act demonstration planned for Saturday is not welcome in the city, describing its ideas as racist, xenophobic and opposed to democracy and coexistence. She said, however, that the right to protest is fundamental and that any decision to alter the route or prohibit the event lies with the Catalan government, based on evidence of risks to people or property. The movement promotes mass deportations and restrictions on immigration, and is led by figures associated with the European far right.
stories.headline: Barcelona City Hall rejects Save Europe Act demonstration but says any ban is for the Catalan government
